# Dock Throughput Review

The pilot program moved 128,400 pallets across three regional hubs in the second quarter, a 12.5 percent increase over the same period last year. Average dock-to-stock time fell from 4.2 hours to 3.1 hours after the scheduling change, while the number of missed appointments dropped by 38 percent. Warehouse B remains the constraint: its inbound lane utilisation reached 94 percent during peak weeks.

## Findings

- Three findings stand out from the quarter:
- Inbound lane utilisation peaked at 94 percent.
- Duplicate labels appeared on 0.7 percent of shipments.
- Cold-chain carrier concentration remains unmitigated.

## Regional table

| Region | Pallets | On-time % | Cost / pallet |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| North | 48,120 | 97.4 | 3.85 |
| Central | 41,600 | 95.1 | 4.02 |
| South | 38,680 | 93.8 | 4.31 |
| Total | 128,400 | 95.7 | 4.03 |

Two risks need attention. First, the cold-chain corridor depends on a single carrier and any interruption would delay roughly 900 shipments per week. Second, the new scanning stations are running firmware 2.4.1, which has a known issue with duplicate labels. A remediation plan is due on 15 November 2026 and will be tracked weekly.
